title: On routine lab reads, GPT-6 Astra scores 66.7%
friendlyTitle: A new test scores how well models read lab results
summary: BioBasicsBench is 100 tasks built with Ligo from raw wet-lab evidence, such as gel images, plates, and instrument files. At the highest reported reasoning setting, GPT-6 Astra earned 66.7% of available credit, against 43.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol. OpenAI says the gain is mostly in reading images and knowing when the evidence is not enough.
friendlySummary: OpenAI tested models on 100 ordinary lab tasks, using real photos and instrument files. The best score shown was 66.7 out of 100. An older model scored 43.8.
whyItMatters: A wrong read of a control can send a scientist down a dead experiment. The benchmark is a score on interpretation, not a lab assistant you should trust unsupervised. Better reading of experimental evidence is useful. It is not permission to run the experiment.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A wrong reading can waste the next experiment. The test measures reading, not doing the lab work. A person still has to check the result.
